register.name: International bank financing with an African Development Fund guarantee
register.detail: Closed 18 September 2026 · 12-year final maturity · African Development Fund partial credit guarantee · Second-loss insurance from the IsDB Group’s insurance subsidiary
register.note: About FCFA 328 billion
register.text: A €500 million loan from international banks to the Republic of Benin, backed by a partial credit guarantee from the African Development Fund. It finances education, health, access to water, infrastructure, renewable energy, agriculture and jobs for young people and women: six of the seven standards in one loan.

register.name: Inaugural international sukuk
register.detail: Issued 22 January 2026 · 7 years · Coupon of 4.92% in euros after a dollar-euro hedge of the full amount
register.note: The first inaugural international sukuk by an African State, in the Ministry’s words
register.text: Benin’s first sukuk, Islamic finance certificates sold to international investors, with a seven-year maturity. A simultaneous dollar-euro hedge of the full amount gives it a coupon of 4.92% in euros.

register.name: Dogo-Bis Multipurpose Dam, Phase 1
register.detail: IDA · Approved 16 June 2026
register.text: Phase 1 of a dam programme with an overall envelope of $580 million.
register.note: Overall envelope $580 million

register.name: Alafia 1, Feeding Benin for the Future
register.detail: IDA and GFF · Approved 16 June 2026
register.text: Nutrition, health and early childhood services for women and children: $150 million from IDA and $20 million from the Global Financing Facility.

register.name: Extended Fund Facility and Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved July 2022 · Seventh and final review completed 25 February 2026 · SDR 484 million in all
register.note: About $36.3 million of it released on the final review
register.text: Benin’s IMF-supported programme of 2022 to 2026, completed with its seventh and final review. Over the programme the fiscal deficit fell to 3.1% of GDP in 2024, and the IMF revised central government debt to 60.5% of GDP at end-2024.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: Approved December 2023 · Fourth and final review completed 25 February 2026 · SDR 148.6 million in all
register.note: About $81.6 million of it released on the final review
register.text: The IMF’s long-term financing for reforms that build resilience to climate change, completed with its fourth and final review. Climate resilience protects the harvests, water and homes behind the seven standards.

register.name: Women entrepreneurs (WEDAF)
register.detail: IDA · Approved 15 January 2026
register.text: Access to finance and growth for women entrepreneurs in the formal and informal sectors.

register.name: Godomey–Ouidah–Hillacondji road upgrade
register.detail: Signed 12 October 2026, Bangkok · IsDB co-financing · Total cost €576.06 million
register.note: On the Abidjan–Lagos corridor
register.text: Financing to expand and upgrade the road from Godomey through Ouidah to Hillacondji, to improve road safety, cut travel times and transport costs, and strengthen trade along the Abidjan–Lagos corridor. Cheaper transport serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Legume-based farming for soil fertility and food security
register.detail: Signed 12 October 2026, Bangkok · IsDB co-financing · Total cost €20.70 million · Five development poles
register.note: Soil fertility, food security and climate resilience
register.text: Financing to spread legume-based farming, improve soil fertility, strengthen food security and build climate resilience across five development poles. It serves the food standard, where 65.6% of Beninese are moderately or severely food insecure.

register.name: West Africa gas market development
register.detail: IDA · Approved 29 June 2026 · With Côte d’Ivoire and Togo
register.text: Benin’s share of a $140 million regional project to build national gas markets and shared supply.

register.name: Gulf of Guinea Northern Regions Social Cohesion (COSO), additional financing
register.detail: IDA · Approved 25 June 2026 · With Côte d’Ivoire and Togo
register.note: Total for Benin, Côte d’Ivoire and Togo
register.text: Additional financing for community investments, infrastructure, livelihood support and inclusion in the northern regions of the three countries. In Benin, 595 community subprojects have been completed, benefiting over 679,000 people.

register.name: Regional DARES, distributed renewable energy, phase 1
register.detail: Approved 22 June 2026 · With the Central African Republic, Liberia and Sierra Leone · First phase of an $853 million programme
register.note: Total for four countries
register.text: Solar home systems, mini-grids and other off-grid technologies for rural and remote communities. It serves the energy standard, the furthest from reach in Benin.

register.name: Grand Nokoué solid waste
register.detail: Approved 25 March 2026 · Sovereign loan · Up to 18 years · Parallel EIB loan of €35.5 million
register.note: Half of a €71 million programme; the second EBRD project signed in Benin
register.text: A sovereign loan to modernise solid waste management in the Grand Nokoué region, home to about 2.8 million people, with sorting centres, composting plants and landfill upgrades. Clean, safe neighbourhoods serve the shelter standard.

register.name: West Africa Coastal Areas (WACA+), Phase 1
register.detail: IDA, PROBLUE and private capital · Approved 17 March 2026 · With Mauritania
register.text: Coastal protection and blue economy jobs at the Bouche du Roy estuary and the mouth of the Mono river.
register.note: Total for Benin and Mauritania

register.name: Western Africa Regional Digital Integration Program, second operation (WARDIP2)
register.detail: IDA · Approved 10 March 2026 · With Liberia and Sierra Leone
register.note: Total for Benin, Liberia and Sierra Leone
register.text: Upgraded digital infrastructure, a more business-friendly environment and help for businesses to scale across regional markets. It serves the livelihood standard through jobs and trade.

register.name: Rural electrification in Mono, Couffo and Borgou
register.detail: Signed 2025 · Sovereign loan for SBEE · Part of a €173 million programme with AFD, the EIB and an EU grant
register.note: The EBRD’s first financing in sub-Saharan Africa
register.text: Extends and modernises medium- and low-voltage networks to connect 120,000 new households, about 600,000 people, in 750 rural villages and towns. It serves the energy standard, the furthest from reach in Benin.

register.name: Clean Oceans Initiative, Grand Nokoué
register.detail: Approved 11 December 2024 · Signed 23 December 2024 · Total cost about €71 million
register.note: Parallel to the EBRD loan for the same programme
register.text: Financing to modernise solid waste management in the five municipalities of Grand Nokoué: sorting units at 60 collection points, four sorting centres, four composting units, a biogas unit and the securing of two landfills, with a focus on plastic waste. Cleaner, safer neighbourhoods serve the shelter standard.

register.name: Eurobond tap, notes due 2038
register.detail: Issued January 2026 · Reopening of the 7.96% amortising notes due 2038 · 6.19% in euros after a full dollar-euro hedge · Alongside the inaugural sukuk
register.note: Additional notes consolidated into the 2038 series first issued in February 2024
register.text: A reopening of the 2038 Eurobond, priced with the first international sukuk, for the budget and the government’s action programme. The hedge into euros removes the dollar risk on a currency tied to the euro.

register.name: Benin–Togo border road, Ouaké–Kabou corridor
register.detail: Approved 21 May 2026 · African Development Fund loan · About 78.8 km of road rehabilitated · Benin’s part $9.5 million
register.note: Multinational loan; Benin’s segment is $9.5 million
register.text: A loan from the African Development Fund to rehabilitate the road on the Ouaké–Kabou corridor between Benin and Togo. Better roads cut transport costs for farmers and traders and serve the livelihood standard.

register.name: Poultry meat programme, phase 1
register.detail: Approved 10 December 2025 · Abidjan · AfDB loan · Mainly in the Savanes region
register.note: First phase of a programme to transform poultry meat production
register.text: A loan from the African Development Bank Group for the first phase of a programme to raise national production of poultry meat; the AfDB expects 50,000 people in the Savanes region to benefit directly. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Rural drinking water programme
register.detail: Approved December 2024 · AfDB €75.63 million · Africa Growing Together Fund about €43 million
register.note: Joint loan from the AfDB and the China-funded Africa Growing Together Fund
register.text: A loan for drinking water in rural Benin, co-financed by the African Development Bank and the Africa Growing Together Fund it manages. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Economic inclusion of young people, additional financing
register.detail: Approved June 2025 · IDA additional financing · Young people with little or no education
register.note: Additional financing; more than 60,000 vulnerable young people already placed in agri-food value chains and wage jobs
register.text: Additional IDA financing for the World Bank’s youth inclusion project, which trains and places young people with little or no schooling in agri-food value chains and wage jobs. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Grand Nokoué urban mobility
register.detail: Approved 20 May 2025 · IDA · Safe, reliable and less polluting public transport
register.note: Public transport for Cotonou and the Grand Nokoué area
register.text: IDA financing to build a safer, more reliable and less polluting public transport system in the Grand Nokoué area around Cotonou. It serves the livelihood standard by bringing jobs and services within reach.

register.name: Land tenure security and integrated forest management
register.detail: Approved 30 April 2025 · Two IDA financings · $100 million Program-for-Results for Terra Benin, the national land tenure programme
register.note: Two operations: land tenure and forest management
register.text: Two IDA financings approved by the World Bank Board: one for Terra Benin, the national land tenure programme, and one for integrated forest management. Secure title to land serves the shelter and livelihood standards.

register.name: Gulf of Guinea Northern Regions Social Cohesion, additional financing (2025)
register.detail: Approved 1 March 2025 · IDA additional financing · Northern Benin, including refugees
register.note: Additional financing for social cohesion and refugees in the north
register.text: Additional IDA financing to strengthen resilience and social cohesion and reduce the vulnerability of refugees and host communities in northern Benin. It serves the livelihood standard; it is separate from the additional financing of June 2026.

register.name: Commercial loan with an IDA guarantee
register.detail: Signed January 2025 · Deutsche Bank · About 6% fixed over 15 years with five years’ grace · IDA guarantee of €200 million · Second-loss cover from ATIDI
register.note: Reported as €507.5 million; the first IDA guarantee under the World Bank Group Guarantee Platform
register.text: A loan from Deutsche Bank to the Government, guaranteed in part by the World Bank’s IDA, used partly to buy back 2032 Eurobonds. It lowers debt service and lengthens maturities, leaving more room for spending on the seven standards.

register.name: Eurobond, 16 years
register.detail: Priced 16 January 2025 · 16-year term · 6.48% in euros after a full currency hedge · Order book seven times the offer · Concurrent tender for the 2032 notes
register.note: Part of about $1 billion raised in January 2025
register.text: A Eurobond issued with a tender offer for part of the outstanding €700 million 4.875% notes due 2032. It extends the debt profile at a fixed euro cost.

register.name: Growth and social and climate resilience package
register.detail: Approved 31 October 2024 · IDA · Private sector-led growth, domestic revenue, social and climate resilience
register.note: IDA package of €635.5 million
register.text: A World Bank package to support the Government’s efforts to strengthen private sector-led growth, raise domestic revenue and build social and climate resilience. It serves the livelihood standard and the public spending behind all seven.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Farmland that already feeds the sub-region and grows its cotton.
items.alt: Cotton fields with white bolls on the northern savanna, Benin

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.
items.alt: Tropical forest with light through the canopy, Benin

items.name: The Coast
items.label: Committed to the coast with Mauritania, 2026
items.text: An Atlantic shoreline and a port economy, now protected and financed as a blue economy.
items.alt: A palm-lined Atlantic beach with a distant port, Benin

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A calm lake with distant pirogues and stilt houses at dawn, Benin

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 41.3% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A colourful market street in Cotonou, Benin

items.name: Tolaro Global
items.text: A cashew processor in Parakou that handled about 6,000 tonnes of raw cashews a year and employed more than 600 people in 2021.

items.name: UDUMA
items.text: A rural water operator in a consortium that won two of the three regional lease contracts to run piped water systems in rural Benin.

items.name: ENGIE Energy Access
items.text: Sells solar home systems on pay-as-you-go terms of about 20 cents a day; an EIB-backed plan aims to deploy 107,000 systems in Benin.

items.name: Kea Medicals
items.text: A Beninese start-up that gives patients a digital medical identity and record on a QR-code bracelet; it counted more than 100,000 registered users in July 2020.

items.name: Gozem
items.text: A transport and payments app working in Benin, Togo, Gabon and Cameroon that finances vehicles for drivers; it raised $30 million in 2025.
